doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Hubert Laws, his doctoral paper and work with Oliver Nelson
summary: They share a love of Hubert Laws; Nelson Jr. wrote his doctoral paper on him, notes Laws played on his father's albums, and presented him the paper.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Wow. You and I — not to get off the track but I noticed you and I share a love of Hubert Laws.

Oh yeah. And I actually did my doctoral paper on Hubert. And I’ve met him several times because he did a lot of work for Dad. He played on the Count Basie “Afrique” album, he played on an album called “The Mayor Speaks” and Dad wrote a suite for strings and jazz orchestra and Hubert played on that. Then he did some television stuff that he would go to L.A. and play. He actually played my first Bundy flute and that was a real treat. So I got a chance to kind of catch back up with him, and actually he was

playing with the Smithsonian, that was a couple of years ago, and I got a chance to actually present my paper to him and I gave him a copy of it. And it was really neat because he said, “This is one of the best papers on me that I’ve ever seen.”
So, and he’s a beautiful player but a beautiful cat.
Um hum. That “Wildflowers” LP that I just think has got it all.
